raw_text:
Below is a safe, 12-week general fitness programme for a 58-year-old man, 6 months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise. The plan keeps heart rate below about 115 bpm (roughly 70% age-predicted max), avoids Valsalva maneuvers, and prohibits max lifts. It uses a full gym, with a focus on gradual progression, technique, and recovery. Use a heart-rate monitor or the talk-test to stay in the intended intensity, and stop immediately if chest pain, dizziness, severe shortness of breath, or any other concerning symptoms occur. All progression is guided by tolerance; if anything feels off, stay at the prior week’s level and consult the prescribing clinician.

How to read the plan
- Each week has: cardio sessions (C), resistance sessions (R), core/balance, and recovery notes.
- Cardio targets: aim for moderate intensity with a steady state effort. If using HR, stay below 115 bpm; if using RPE, aim around 11–13 (some days 12–14 if well tolerated but never to feel breathless). Use the talk test as a practical guide.
- Resistance targets: use machines first, then light free weights. 2–3 sets of 10–15 reps early, moving toward 3 sets of 8–12 reps as tolerated. No max lifts.
- Rest: 1–2 minutes between sets for resistance work; longer rest if needed for technique.
- Progression: small, continuous improvements in sets, reps, or weight every week or two, based on tolerance and form.

Phase overview
- Weeks 1–3: Foundation and technique (easy-to-moderate cardio; light resistance with emphasis on form).
- Weeks 4–6: Build volume and endurance (slightly longer cardio; more resistance work; begin split routines).
- Weeks 7–9: Build strength endurance and consistency (three resistance days per week; steady cardio volume).
- Weeks 10–12: Solidify routine and prepare for sustainable long-term fitness (consistent four sessions/week; modest load increases; balanced recovery).

Week-by-week plan

Week 1
- Focus: Establish routine, learn safe technique.
- Cardio (3 days: Mon/Wed/Fri)
  - 20–25 minutes continuous, comfortable pace.
  - Modality: treadmill walking, stationary bike, or elliptical.
  - Intensity: aim HR <115 bpm or RPE 11–12.
  - Warm-up 4–5 minutes; cool-down 4–5 minutes with gentle walking or cycling.
- Resistance (2 days: Tue/Thu)
  - Machines only; full-body circuit.
  - Exercises: Leg press, Leg extension, Leg curl, Calf raise, Chest press, Seated row, Lat pulldown, Shoulder press.
  - Load/volume: 2 sets x 12–15 reps per exercise; 60–90 seconds rest.
  - Technique cue: exhale on exertion; no breath-holding.
- Core/Mobility: 5–10 minutes post-workout (bird dog, dead bug, pelvic tilts).
- Recovery: 1–2 days light activity (walking, gentle mobility work); prioritize sleep.

Week 2
- Focus: Increase familiarity; gentle progression.
- Cardio (3 days)
  - 20–30 minutes; HR <115 bpm or RPE 11–13.
  - Same modalities; progress by 5 minutes total across the week if comfortable.
- Resistance (2 days)
  - Same exercises; keep 2 sets x 12–15 reps; small weight increase only if technique is solid.
- Core/Mobility: 5–10 minutes; add simple thoracic mobility (thread-the-needle, wall slides).
- Recovery: as Week 1.

Week 3
- Focus: Slightly higher volume; begin light load progression.
- Cardio (3 days)
  - 25–30 minutes; HR still under 115 bpm, or RPE 12.
- Resistance (3 days, Tue/Thu/Sat)
  - Split into two upper-lower circuits:
    - Upper body: Chest press, Seated row, Lat pulldown, Shoulder press.
    - Lower body: Leg press, Leg extension, Leg curl, Calf raise.
  - Load/volume: 2 sets x 12–12 reps (upper and lower). If technique is solid, progress to 3 sets x 10–12 reps on one or two exercises.
- Core/Mobility: 6–12 minutes total (include side planks if comfortable, otherwise modify).
- Recovery: maintain and monitor symptoms; adjust if needed.

Week 4
- Phase start: Increase structure; begin a simple upper/lower split.
- Cardio (3 days)
  - 30 minutes continuous at HR <115 bpm or RPE 12.
  - Include one day of 30–40 minutes if tolerated.
- Resistance (3 days: Tue/Thu/Sat)
  - Upper body day: Chest press, Seated row, Lat pulldown, Shoulder press; 3 sets x 10–12 reps.
  - Lower body day: Leg press, Leg extension, Leg curl, Calf raise; 3 sets x 10–12 reps.
  - Core: add 2 core sets (e.g., dead bug, bird dog) at the end of one session.
- Mobility/Recovery: 8–12 minutes of mobility work after each session.

Week 5
- Focus: Small progression in resistance; cardio stability.
- Cardio (3 days)
  - 30–35 minutes; HR <115 bpm; maintain comfortable pace.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - Keep upper/lower split; aim for 3 sets x 10–12 reps; increase weight modestly on 1–2 exercises where technique remains solid.
- Core/Balance: 8–12 minutes (include side planks or bird-dog variations).
- Recovery: same guidelines.

Week 6
- Focus: Stabilize routine; modest overload.
- Cardio (3 days)
  - 30–40 minutes; same intensity rules.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - Upper body: 3 sets x 10–12 reps; progress to 3x12 on 1 exercise if feasible.
  - Lower body: 3 sets x 10–12 reps; progress to 3x12 on 1 exercise if feasible.
- Core/Balance: 10–12 minutes featuring controlled planks and hip hinges.
- Recovery: maintain sleep and hydration; daily light activity encouraged.

Week 7
- Phase: Maintain momentum; introduce circuit-style resistance for variety.
- Cardio (3–4 days)
  - 35–45 minutes total across the week, staying under the HR cap.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - Circuit format: choose 6–8 exercises (upper/lower/hinge/push-pull) and perform one set back-to-back in a circuit, rest 60–90 seconds between circuits. 2 circuits to start; progress to 3 circuits as tolerated.
  - Reps: 10–12 per exercise; load kept at a moderate level with safe technique.
- Core/Balance: 10–12 minutes after sessions.
- Recovery: emphasize active recovery days.

Week 8
- Focus: Consolidation; maintain progress with stable form.
- Cardio (3–4 days)
  - 35–45 minutes; HR target as before.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - Maintain circuit approach or switch to upper/lower split with 3 sets x 10–12 reps.
  - Add light progression to 5–10% weight where form allows.
- Core/Balance: 10–15 minutes.
- Recovery: consistent sleep and hydration.

Week 9
- Focus: Prepare for continued long-term fitness; refine technique.
- Cardio (3–4 days)
  - 40–45 minutes total; keep intensity moderate.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - Upper/lower split or full-body circuits; 3 sets x 10–12 reps; progression in small increments.
- Core/Balance: 12–15 minutes; add a few stability-based moves (dead bug with shorter levers, bird-dog with longer hold if comfortable).
- Recovery: maintain.

Week 10
- Focus: Stability and readiness for ongoing routine; consider small loading increases.
- Cardio (4 days)
  - 40–50 minutes total; consistent, comfortable pace.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - 3 sets x 8–12 reps; add slight weight increases where technique remains precise; keep Valsalva-free.
- Core/Balance: 12–15 minutes.
- Recovery: emphasize tapering down if fatigue accumulates; otherwise keep steady.

Week 11
- Focus: Steady-state conditioning and strength endurance.
- Cardio (4 days)
  - 40–50 minutes at moderate intensity.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - Full-body or upper/lower split; 3 sets x 8–12 reps; progression in small increments.
- Core/Balance: 12–15 minutes.
- Recovery: prioritize sleep and nutrition.

Week 12
- Focus: Consolidation and plan for maintenance beyond the program.
- Cardio (4 days)
  - 40–50 minutes; keep HR under limit.
- Resistance (3 days)
  - 3 sets x 8–12 reps; aim for a modest, sustainable load increase vs. Week 11 if form is solid.
- Core/Balance: 12–15 minutes; include a brief balance circuit.
- Recovery: set a plan for ongoing activity 3–4 days/week, with 1–2 days of mobility/rest.

Nutrition, recovery, and behavior notes (throughout the 12 weeks)
- Protein: aim for roughly 1.2–1.6 g/kg body weight per day to support muscle maintenance and recovery. Distribute protein evenly across meals.
- Carbohydrates: choose complex carbohydrates (vegetables, whole grains, fruits) to fuel workouts; adjust intake to support energy needs without excessive weight gain.
- Fats: emphasize heart-healthy fats (olive oil, nuts, seeds, fatty fish). Limit saturated fats and avoid trans fats.
- Fiber: include 25–38 g/day, unless medically advised otherwise.
- Hydration: target regular fluid intake; adjust for activity level and climate.
- Sodium: general heart-healthy approach; follow clinician guidance (often modest sodium reduction is advised, but this should be tailored).
- Alcohol: if consumed, do so in moderation and with clinician guidance.
- Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours per night to support recovery and heart health.
- Recovery strategies: include light mobility work on rest days, foam rolling if tolerated, warm bath or gentle stretching, and breathing work (diaphragmatic breathing) to help with autonomic balance.
- Monitoring and safety: always check in with the client’s physician if there are any signs of angina, unusually shortness of breath, dizziness, leg swelling that worsens, or chest pain during or after exercise. Use the RPE and talk test to gauge effort; do not progress if technique is compromised or the client reports adverse symptoms.

Equipment and safety reminders
- Start with machines for resistance to minimize form risk; progress to free weights only when technique and cardiovascular tolerance are solid.
- Avoid exercises that require breath-holding or excessive intra-abdominal pressure.
- Ensure a safe, well-ventilated gym environment; have a staff member or trainer present for initial weeks if possible, particularly during resistance sessions.
- Gradual progression is key: add small reps, sets, or light weight every 1–2 weeks depending on tolerance and form.

This plan aims to deliver a balanced, sustainable 12-week path to general fitness while respecting the client’s cardiac status. If you want, I can tailor the weekly sessions to match a specific gym layout (equipment availability), or adjust the progression pace based on his real-time tolerance and feedback.
